title: Spotter's Challenge
scoring: 3 points for a first-try answer, 2 for second, 1 for third, 0 if missed.
note: TEST build: answers are in this file. The live version should check answers server-side (see LEADERBOARD-PLAN.md).

puzzles.question: Which exact 777 variant is this?
clues: Start with the wingtip, then count the door pairs.
It has the GE90-115B, the only engine offered on this variant.
The best-selling 777 version by far, and a daily sight at LAX.
puzzles.tell: Raked wingtips plus the long fuselage with five door pairs. The -300 has the same length but no raked tips; the -200LR has raked tips but only four door pairs.
puzzles.fact: United 777-300ER on final at Washington Dulles. Registration and fleet number blurred so you cannot look it up.

puzzles.question: Name the engine on this 747.
clues: Look at the trailing edge of the fan nozzle.
Only one 747 version could have this engine, and it first flew in 2010.
A bleed-air sibling of one of the 787's two engine choices.
puzzles.tell: Chevrons (the sawtooth trailing edge) on the nacelle. Of the 747's engine options, only the 747-8's GEnx-2B has them; CF6, PW4000 and RB211 nacelles have smooth edges.
puzzles.fact: Nippon Cargo Airlines 747-8F JA13KZ on approach to Tokyo Narita. The engine name printed on the nacelles is blurred.

puzzles.question: Which SoCal airport is this?
clues: The building opened in 1941 and is a protected landmark.
The control tower sits on top of the terminal itself.
Its runway 30 is the longest on the field and its airline slots are capped by a local noise ordinance.
puzzles.tell: The 1941 Streamline Moderne terminal with its rooftop tower and porthole windows. Burbank's terminal is a 1930 Spanish Revival building and ONT and SBA have modern terminals.
puzzles.fact: Long Beach's historic terminal now serves as the ticketing building; gates are in the newer concourse behind it. The airport name on the facade is blurred.

puzzles.question: Exact 737 variant? Type it in.
clues: Count the exits behind the wing.
LEAP-1B engines with chevroned nacelles and split-tip winglets.
Longer than the -8, shorter than the -10.
puzzles.tell: The mid-cabin exit door (a plugged door on Alaska's jets) just behind the wing. The 737-8 does not have it; the 737-900ER has it too but has CFM56 engines with smooth nacelles and no split-tip winglets.

puzzles.question: This 747 later became NASA 905. Who was its first operator?
clues: It is a 747-100, delivered new in 1970.
Boeing's customer code in its model number is 23.
Its original registration was N9668.
puzzles.tell: The model number. NASA 905 is a 747-123, and the '23' customer code belongs to American Airlines. NASA bought it in 1974.
puzzles.fact: In September 2012 NASA 905 carried Space Shuttle Endeavour on its final ferry flight into LAX, with a low pass over SoCal on the way.

puzzles.question: Close-up of the main gear. Which aircraft?
clues: Count the wheels on one main gear leg.
Airbus stretched this one by about 7 m and gave it a stronger gear.
Launch operator was Qatar Airways in 2018.
puzzles.tell: Six-wheel main bogies. The A350-900, A330neo and 787-10 all use four-wheel bogies.
puzzles.fact: This photo shows the first A350-1000 delivered. Launch customer Qatar Airways took it in February 2018.

puzzles.question: Three of these jets had their final assembly in Southern California. Which one did not?
clues: The TriStar in the photo is one of the three.
Think Long Beach and Palmdale.
The odd one out was built alongside the 737 in Washington state.
puzzles.tell: The 757 came off Boeing's Renton, Washington line. TriStars were assembled at Lockheed's Palmdale plant; the MD-11 and 717 at Douglas (later Boeing) Long Beach.
puzzles.fact: The last airliner built in Long Beach was a 717 for AirTran in 2006; the C-17 line there closed in 2015.

puzzles.question: Which exact variant is this airBaltic jet?
clues: Judge the cabin length against the size of the engines.
airBaltic's entire jet fleet is a single type and a single length.
It is the longer of the two versions Bombardier designed as the CSeries.
puzzles.tell: The big PW1500G geared turbofans under a clean, slim wing and the long cabin. The A220-300 is 3.7 m longer than the -100, the E195-E2 has a different nose and tail, and the A319neo has wingtip sharklets.
puzzles.fact: airBaltic flies only the A220-300 and was its launch operator in December 2016, when the type was still called the Bombardier CS300. Registration blurred.

puzzles.question: Name the engine family on this Cathay Pacific A330-300.
clues: Rule out the A330neo-only option first.
Cathay picked the British option for every A330 it ordered.
Cathay Pacific was the launch operator of this engine in 1995.
puzzles.tell: This is an A330ceo, so the neo-only Trent 7000 is out, and Cathay Pacific specified the Trent 700 for all of its A330s. Expert spotters also look for the Trent's long, full-length nacelle.
puzzles.fact: The Trent 700 entered service with Cathay Pacific on the A330 in 1995, the first member of the Trent family to fly with an airline.

puzzles.question: Which Southern California airport terminal is this?
clues: Read the landscape, not the building.
Low desert scrub, palms and bare mountains close behind the field.
It sits at the foot of Mount San Jacinto, with open-air gate areas on the ramp.
puzzles.tell: The white tent-style canopies over the terminal plus the open Coachella Valley desert and mountains right behind it. ONT and BUR sit in built-up valleys, and SAN is on San Diego Bay.
puzzles.fact: Palm Springs International is the main airline airport for the Coachella Valley. Its original terminal was designed by desert modernist architect Donald Wexler and opened in 1965.

puzzles.question: Exact 787 variant? Type it in.
clues: Compare the cabin length behind the wing to the length ahead of it.
The longest Dreamliner, a simple stretch of the -9.
United is its largest US operator and Singapore Airlines took the first one.
puzzles.tell: A very long, slender fuselage with an extra-long aft cabin. The 787-10 is 5.5 m longer than the -9 and 11.6 m longer than the -8, with the same wing.
puzzles.fact: The 787-10 first flew in March 2017 and entered service with Singapore Airlines in April 2018. Registration, fleet number and the 787 lettering are blurred.

puzzles.question: This NASA 747SP flying observatory was based in Palmdale. Who was its first operator?
clues: It was delivered new in 1977.
Its first owner named it Clipper Lindbergh.
It later flew for United before NASA bought it.
puzzles.tell: SOFIA (N747NA) began life with Pan Am as Clipper Lindbergh, moved to United when Pan Am sold its Pacific routes, and was bought by NASA in 1997.
puzzles.fact: SOFIA carried a 2.5 m infrared telescope behind a door in its rear fuselage. It flew its last science mission in 2022 and is now displayed at the Pima Air and Space Museum in Tucson.

puzzles.question: Which exact variant is this narrowbody?
clues: Count the doors and look how far the fuselage runs behind the wing.
Only 55 of this version were built.
Launch customer was the German leisure airline Condor in 1999.
puzzles.tell: A 757 wing and nose, but a far longer fuselage stretching well behind the wing. The 757-300 is about 7 m longer than the -200, which makes it the longest single-aisle twin jet built.
puzzles.fact: Delta inherited its 757-300s from Northwest. Registration and fleet numbers blurred.

puzzles.question: Which regional jet is this?
clues: Compare the nose with the engine diameter. The titles are not the type.
Those nacelles are much wider than a CF34.
The nose is longer than a first-generation E-Jet. An A220 radome is rounder.
puzzles.tell: The E195-E2 pairs a longer, more pointed nose with Pratt & Whitney PW1900G geared turbofans. The E175 and the first-generation E195 use smaller CF34s. The A220-300 also has a geared turbofan, but its nose and windshield are rounder.
puzzles.fact: KLM Cityhopper E195-E2. The E2 wing is a new, longer wing, and the engine is the PW1900G rather than the CF34-10E of the E195. Registration blurred.

credit.title: KLM Cityhopper Embraer E195-E2 PH-NXB at Schiphol 24-11-2022.jpg
credit.changes: Resized to 900 px wide, all embedded metadata (EXIF/XMP) stripped; zoomed crops shown during play. Registration blurred.

puzzles.question: Which business jet is this?
clues: Count the oval cabin windows, then look at the tail.
There are eight large ovals, and no engine in the fin.
The G550 has seven smaller windows. Global 7500 windows are rectangular. The Falcon 8X is a trijet.
puzzles.tell: Eight large oval cabin windows and a clean tail. The G550 has seven, and they are smaller. The Global 7500's windows are bigger rectangles. The Falcon 8X carries a third engine in the tail.
puzzles.fact: EC-LZU is a 2013 Gulfstream G650, c/n 6066. The G650ER is the same shape with more range, so the window count is the family tell. Registration on the tail blurred.

credit.title: EC-LZU Gulfstream G650 SCQ.jpg

puzzles.question: Three of these can wear this wingtip. Which cannot?
clues: Look at the blade under the tip, not only the tall blue piece.
This is an Aviation Partners split scimitar, a retrofit for the 737NG.
The 737 MAX leaves the factory with a different tip, the Advanced Technology winglet.
puzzles.tell: The lower ventral blade plus the hooked cap is the Split Scimitar Winglet, certified for the 737-700, 737-800, 737-900 and 737-900ER. The 737-8 uses Boeing's Advanced Technology winglet instead.
puzzles.fact: Split scimitars are a retrofit of the older blended winglet, not a MAX part. A second aircraft in the original frame, with a different scimitar tip, was cropped out.

credit.title: Boeing 737 and 757 scimitar winglets comparison.jpg
credit.changes: Cropped to the near split-scimitar wingtip, resized to 900 px wide, all embedded metadata (EXIF/XMP) stripped; zoomed crops shown during play.

puzzles.question: Which engine is under this wing?
clues: Look at the nozzle. Is the trailing edge sawtoothed or smooth?
The nacelle is large and round, and the nozzle has no chevrons.
Chevrons would make it a LEAP. A flattened bottom would make it the 737 MAX's LEAP-1B.
puzzles.tell: A fat round nacelle and a smooth nozzle. That is the PW1100G family. The LEAP-1A is also big and round, but its nozzle is chevroned. The LEAP-1B is flattened underneath. The CFM56-5B is a smaller, longer nacelle.
puzzles.fact: Lufthansa A320neo D-AINU is an A320-271N. Its PW1127G is a thrust rating in the PW1100G family. In Airbus's three-digit engine code, the 1 means Pratt & Whitney.

credit.title: D-AINU A320neo Lufthansa PW1100G SCQ.jpg
credit.changes: Resized to 900 px wide, all embedded metadata (EXIF/XMP) stripped; zoomed crops shown during play.

puzzles.question: Where is this aircraft registered?
clues: Read the marks on the engine, including the letter after the hyphen.
Several island registers share the VP- prefix. The next letter is the one that matters.
VP-C is the Cayman Islands. Bermuda is VP-B, and the British Virgin Islands are VP-L.
puzzles.tell: The cowling reads VP-CPT. Cayman Islands marks are VP-C followed by two letters. Bermuda uses VP-B and VQ-B, so VP- alone is not enough.
puzzles.fact: The Isle of Man register uses M-, not VP-. This Global 6000 wears Cayman marks. The registration was left readable on purpose.

credit.title: Bombardier BD-700 Global Express 6000 ‘VP-CPT’.jpg
credit.changes: Resized to 900 px wide, all embedded metadata (EXIF/XMP) stripped; zoomed crops shown during play. Registration left readable.

puzzles.question: Which airline and type is this?
clues: The windshield is shared with another Boeing. Judge the fuselage width beside it.
The titles on the forward fuselage name the airline. The body is too wide for a 757.
This is the widebody that uses the 757 flight deck. An A330 nose and a 737 nose do not match these windows.
puzzles.tell: Boeing gave the 767 and the 757 the same windshield. The 767's fuselage is much wider, which shows in the cheek beside the jetway. Delta's widget is on the forward fuselage.
puzzles.fact: N194DN is a Delta 767-332, the airline's 767-300ER. The A330's cockpit mask is a different shape, and the 737 nose is smaller.

credit.title: Delta Boeing 767-300ER N194DN at Boston May 2025.jpg
credit.changes: Resized to 900 px wide, all embedded metadata (EXIF/XMP) stripped; zoomed crops shown during play.

puzzles.question: Which exact variant is this?
clues: Find the door just behind the wing before you decide from the engine.
The 737-800 and the 737-8 do not have that extra exit.
The nacelle is a round CFM56 with a smooth lip, not a chevroned LEAP.
puzzles.tell: An extra exit just aft of the wing, plus a round CFM56 rather than a LEAP. The 737-9 has the same door, but its LEAP-1B nacelle is flattened on the bottom and ends in chevrons.
puzzles.fact: Delta 737-900ER. That mid-exit door is the stretch that separates the 737-900ER from the 737-800. Registration blurred.

puzzles.question: Which classic airliner family is this?
clues: Count the engines, then look at the landing gear.
Two radial engines, a tailwheel, one rounded fin, and a slim fuselage, not the C-46's deep, bulging one.
This exact airplane is on the list for tomorrow's Flabob Veterans Celebration.
puzzles.tell: Twin radials, a tailwheel and a single rounded fin. The C-46 is much bigger with a deep, bulging fuselage, the Lodestar has twin tail fins, and the Convair 240 sits on a nosewheel.
puzzles.fact: N103NA "Flabob Express" appears on Wikimedia Commons as both a DC-3 and a C-47B; the C-47 is the military version of the DC-3. Flabob lists the Flabob Express DC-3 for its Veterans Celebration on Sat, Nov 14. Photo from June 9, 2019.

credit.title: Douglas DC-3 N103NA Flabob Express (48105191588).jpg

puzzles.question: Which light helicopter is this?
clues: Count the main rotor blades.
Four blades on a LongRanger-style cabin with big side windows.
Bell just delivered the 2,000th of this model.
puzzles.tell: A four-blade main rotor on a LongRanger-shaped cabin. The 206L LongRanger has a two-blade rotor, the H125 a three-blade rotor and a different nose, and the MD 500E is a much smaller egg-shaped helicopter.
puzzles.fact: N462P is a 2014 Bell 407 (serial 54164) owned by PHI Health, per its Commons description, photographed Feb 24, 2021. Bell delivered its 2,000th 407 to White Saddle Air Services in British Columbia (AviTrader, Nov 9, 2026).

puzzles.question: Which SoCal airport is this?
clues: Look at what sits next to the field and how close downtown is.
Open water sits right behind the gates.
It has a single runway and is fully closed 1:00 to 6:00 AM PT on Sun Nov 15 and Mon Nov 16 for work.
puzzles.tell: Gates backed right up against the bay, next to downtown. None of Long Beach, John Wayne or Burbank has its gates backed onto open water.
puzzles.fact: Aerial photo of San Diego International Airport, Feb 28, 2022. SAN is fully closed Sun Nov 15 and Mon Nov 16 from 1:00 to 6:00 AM PT (NOTAMs 11/043 and 11/048).

puzzles.question: Which exact variant is this JetBlue jet?
clues: First decide A320 or A321: count the doors along the fuselage.
There are extra doors ahead of and behind the wing, so it is the long one.
Now look at the engine size. These nacelles are slim, not the fat new-engine kind.
puzzles.tell: The A321 adds a door ahead of and behind the wing that the A320 does not have. The A321neo and A321XLR use much larger LEAP-1A or PW1100G nacelles, so slimmer engines point to the ceo.
puzzles.fact: JetBlue A321ceo N980JT landing on Runway 27 at San Diego, Feb 18, 2019, per its Commons description. JetBlue restarts daily SAN to Fort Lauderdale on Nov 19 with the A321ceo (Simple Flying, Nov 9).

credit.title: JetBlueA321ceoN980JT SANFebruary2019.jpg
credit.changes: Resized; embedded metadata stripped; zoomed crops shown during play. Registration left readable.

puzzles.question: Which business jet is this?
clues: Look at the window shape, then the length of the cabin.
Large rounded-rectangle windows, not Gulfstream ovals.
This is Bombardier's flagship four-zone Global, with more windows than a Global 6000.
puzzles.tell: Bombardier windows and a very long cabin. The Global 6000 is noticeably shorter with fewer windows, and the G700 and G650 have Gulfstream's big oval windows.
puzzles.fact: CS-ESS, a 2021 Global 7500, on final at Baltimore/Washington International, May 20, 2025, per its Commons description. Bombardier's backlog reached $22.2 billion (Instajet).

puzzles.question: Which rotorcraft is this?
clues: Count the rotors.
Two rotors, front and back, and four landing-gear legs.
A civil one was scheduled to fly along Santa Monica Beach for Veterans Day.
puzzles.tell: Tandem rotors on a big boxy fuselage with four landing-gear legs. The CH-46 also has tandem rotors but is smaller and sits on three landing-gear legs, the CH-53E has one main rotor, and the V-22 tilts its rotors on wingtips.
puzzles.fact: U.S. Army CH-47F hovering at Frederick Municipal Airport, Maryland, Nov 6, 2024, per its Commons description. Coulson Aviation was set to fly a Chinook and a C-130 along the Santa Monica shoreline on Veterans Day (Yo! Venice, Nov 10).

credit.title: U.S. Army Boeing CH-47F Chinook 11-08097 FDK MD1.jpg
credit.changes: Resized; embedded metadata stripped; zoomed crops shown during play. Registration left readable.

puzzles.question: Which airline and type is this?
clues: Four engines and a hump. Now look at the wingtips.
No upturned winglets: the wingtips are swept back.
The engines have sawtooth chevrons at the back.
puzzles.tell: A 747 hump with raked wingtips and chevroned GEnx engines. The 747-400 has upturned winglets and the A340-600 has no hump. The crane on the tail and the titles say Lufthansa, not Air China.
puzzles.fact: D-ABYL, a 2014 Lufthansa 747-8, approaching Washington Dulles, March 22, 2026, per its Commons description. Lufthansa's first A350-1000 arrived in Munich on Nov 11 (Lufthansa Group).
